thread.title: Trump: Stock market turbulence ‘big mistake’

author: Mike Sunnucks
title: Trump: Stock market turbulence ‘big mistake’
text: – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Feb 7, 2018, 11:16am MST U.S. President Donald Trump has weighed in on Twitter (NYSE: TWTR) regarding the big drop stocks on Monday and the high volatility of the Dow Jones Industrial Average the past two days. Trump has previously touted record highs for the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq but was quiet on stocks during this week’s turbulence. That changed this morning. “In the “old days,” when good news was reported, the Stock Market would go up. Today, when good news is reported, the Stock Market goes down. Big mistake, and we have so much good (great) news about the economy!,” Trump tweeted. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported last week the U.S. gained 200,000 jobs in January and wages went up 2.9 percent in 2017. The jobs beat analysts' estimates of 180,000 and the wage gains are the best since 2009, according to the Street.com. The unemployment rate in metro Phoenix is 3.9 percent. It’s 4.1 percent nationally, according to BLS. Trump has also touted the tax cuts passed in December that reduce corporate rates and resulted in raises and bonuses from a number of big companies such as Starbucks (Nasdaq: SBUX), Walt Disney Co. (NYSE: DIS) and JPMorgan Chase (NYSE: JPM). Others — such as Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) and Boeing (NYSE: BA) — say they are using tax cut windfalls to boost U.S. investments. They both have operations in Mesa and Chase has a big footprint in downtown Phoenix and is building a big new campus in Tempe. But stocks went down big Friday and went down huge on Monday. Geoffrey Smith, a finance professor and stock market expert at Arizona State University’s W.P. Carey School of Business, said there are concerns the tax cuts will magnify federal deficits and without spending cuts will push up yields on U.S. Treasury notes. Those have already been going up with interest rates rising. Better yields for Treasuries and bonds encourages investors to take money out of stocks, Smith said. “It’s not the tax cuts. It’s the deficit,” Smith said. – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Feb 7, 2018, 11:16am MST
